subject.title: [Bug] web_fetch fails in dual-stack networks when DNS returns IPv6 special-use addresses

question: Should OpenClaw relax the default web_fetch SSRF DNS-answer rule from fail-on-any-blocked-answer to filtered mixed-answer semantics for public hostnames?
rationale: The code change is small, but it changes the default outbound SSRF policy for mixed DNS responses and needs maintainer security intent before automation should alter it.

options.title: Approve Filtered Mixed Answers
options.body: Allow the request only when at least one DNS answer is allowed, remove blocked answers from the pinned pool, and test mixed plus all-blocked cases.

options.title: Keep Any-Blocked Fail-Closed
options.body: Continue treating any blocked DNS answer as a hard stop and document trusted proxy or narrow fake-IP options as the supported workaround.

options.title: Require Explicit Opt-In
options.body: Preserve the current default and add or reuse an operator-controlled policy for polluted DNS environments.

recommendation.title: Approve Filtered Mixed Answers
recommendation.body: Allow the request only when at least one DNS answer is allowed, remove blocked answers from the pinned pool, and test mixed plus all-blocked cases.

likelyOwner.reason: The central SSRF assertion and IPv6 special-use policy history point to this as the strongest available owner for the security-boundary decision.
